markdown_report:
The best next step is **controlled residual restoration**: extend the existing history perturbations with activation patching inside each frozen BERT4Rec. At 10% research progress, this offers a small, testable diagnostic improvement before changing training.

Three starting insights motivate it. First, Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have measured negative-win rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These training-position measurements identify weaker separation but do not establish validation performance. Second, embedding alignment near 0.51 corresponds to mean cosine similarity near zero. It does not support treating global embedding collapse as the primary problem. Third, serving parity and position-preserving perturbations already control important implementation confounds. They establish a foundation for investigating which internal computations transmit history changes.

Three related-work insights refine the proposal. Zhang and Nanda [1] show that activation-patching conclusions depend on corruption and measurement choices. Therefore, use fixed candidates and report raw margin changes across several controlled perturbations. Heimersheim and Nanda [2] distinguish restoration from disruption. Running both directions can expose asymmetric effects without claiming a unique mechanism. Sampled-metric analysis [3] shows that candidate sampling can change model comparisons. Consequently, prefix diagnostics, host validation HR@10, and full-catalog recommendations require separate interpretation.

These insights define three research directions: measurement reliability, computational localization, and validation of diagnostic-guided repairs. The framework is:

| Stage | Intervention or evidence | Permitted conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Reliability | Sampler checks, serving parity, identity patches | Probe consistency |
| Localization | Position-matched corruption and residual patches | Components transmitting score changes |
| Utility | Prespecified repair; pinned host validation | Observed recommendation improvement |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity-patch invariance checks [1,2] | 2/6/2 | Cheap protection against probe errors | Limited scientific novelty |
| Controlled residual restoration [1,2] | 5/8/4 | Localizes effects using the existing checkpoint | Corruption-dependent evidence |
| Gradient-guided, matched token interventions | 4/7/6 | Scales attribution across histories | Gradients and interventions can disagree |

Select residual restoration. For each eligible training prefix, retain the appended MASK, absolute positions, candidates, and eligibility rules. Cache clean and corrupted activations; patch one intermediate layer’s selected history-token residuals in both directions. Measure target-minus-hardest-negative margin changes, target-rank changes, and paired uncertainty. Include identity patches and random token sets matched for size and position range. Report unstable or zero-effect cases explicitly.

Keep one checkpoint per category, preserve all diagnostic interfaces, and restore hooks, model mode, and RNG state. No training improvement or recovered user intent is implied; the next hypothesis must earn support through unchanged macro validation HR@10.

[1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042
[2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255
[3] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/

idea.description: Extend the corrected BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter with bidirectional residual-stream patching between clean histories and position-preserving corrupted histories. Use one frozen trained model per category to identify intermediate computations that transmit measured ranking changes.
idea.motivation: Existing perturbations measure behavioral sensitivity but cannot locate the computations responsible. The supplied diagnostics show weaker training-position separation in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics, while providing no evidence of widespread directional embedding collapse. A controlled localization probe is a feasible early-stage extension; it does not assume that greater history sensitivity improves recommendation quality.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every ModelView interface. Gate patching on sampler and exported-predictor parity checks. Construct clean and corrupted inputs from eligible public training prefixes, keeping candidate IDs, absolute positions, padding conventions, and the appended MASK position fixed. Patch intermediate Transformer block outputs at selected history positions; avoid treating final-readout replacement as explanatory evidence. Run clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption, identity patches, and seeded random-position controls. Define the primary margin as target score minus maximum negative-candidate score; report raw paired changes, ranks, sample counts, and paired-user bootstrap intervals. Avoid normalized recovery when the clean-corrupt difference is near zero. Catch unsupported architecture hooks and return unavailable metrics with reasons. Remove hooks and restore model mode and RNG states even on failure. Maintain exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category, seed 42, preprocessing seed 0, and the fixed training limits and routing. This diagnostic requires no predictor changes, external data, additional fitted models, or test access. Any subsequent training change must preserve BERT4Rec masking and synchronize checkpoint loading with the embedded predictor writer. Selection remains the host's four-category macro validation HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save model mode and RNG states
    try:
        model.eval()
        run existing sampler and serving-parity checks
        if checks fail: return measured metrics and definitions with patching unavailable
        with no_grad():
            for eligible public training prefix:
                clean = serving_input(prefix, appended_MASK=True)
                corrupt = position_preserving_history_corruption(clean)
                candidates = fixed_target_and_99_unique_eligible_negatives(prefix)
                cache clean and corrupt intermediate block outputs
                measure clean and corrupt scores and margins
                for selected intermediate layer and history-token set:
                    restore = score corrupt with clean residuals patched at selected positions
                    disrupt = score clean with corrupt residuals patched at selected positions
                    run identity patches and matched random-position controls
                    record raw margin changes, target ranks, and control differences
            summarize paired user effects separately for each category
            attach definitions, denominators, uncertainty, and unavailable reasons
        return {metrics, metric_definitions}
    finally:
        remove all hooks
        restore model mode and RNG states

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics and definitions
    require separation of observations, computational hypotheses, and validation claims
    prohibit inferred compatibility, current intent, or unavailable user traits

originality.positive: Combines serving-aligned sequential perturbations with controlled, bidirectional activation patching under a single-checkpoint constraint.
originality.negative: Activation patching and matched corruption controls are established methods; novelty lies primarily in their careful BERT4Rec adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Could support falsifiable hypotheses about history processing and guide small, prespecified training repairs.
future_potential.negative: Localization depends on intervention choices and may not predict improvements in the host's validation objective.

code_difficulty.positive: Forward hooks and existing perturbation infrastructure allow implementation without retraining or changing serving.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct residual locations, padding masks, matched controls, and exception-safe cleanup require careful architecture-specific implementation.

related_work.title: Zhang and Nanda: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models
contributions: Studies how corruption choices and evaluation metrics affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates explicit controls and multiple behavioral measurements.
limitations: Provides methodological evidence from language models rather than validation gains for this BERT4Rec benchmark.
Patching results remain dependent on the chosen intervention.

related_work.title: Heimersheim and Nanda: How to use and interpret activation patching
contributions: Motivates complementary restoration and disruption experiments.
limitations: Does not establish a unique or complete mechanism from a single successful patch.
Requires adaptation to sequential recommendation and its masking conventions.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
Supports separate interpretation of diagnostic candidate sets and full-catalog recommendations.
limitations: Does not evaluate the proposed residual-patching diagnostic.
Does not replace the task's mandated pinned validation protocol.
